A person can be moth-keyed in more than.why: "Moth-keyed" is a made-up relation (catalogued as moth_keyed_in, fictional, no property tags): nobody uses the phrase, so it does not occur in Dolma or on Wikipedia, and its words give no default reading about the property inserted here. Unlike "died in" or "was born in", its words name no event, so nothing says a person has only one such year. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

sources.quote: Magna Carta (Medieval Latin for "Great Charter"), sometimes spelled Magna Charta, is a royal charter of rights sealed by King John of England at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215.

Abraham Lincoln was the first president.why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: Lincoln was the 16th president; Washington was the first.

sources.quote: Abraham Lincoln (February 12, 1809 – April 15, 1865) was the 16th president of the United States, from 1861 until his assassination in 1865.

notes: RBox expansion paired with history-replace-0018 (which makes 'died in year' not functional): a made-up relation, moth_keyed_in (person to year), is given the same property, applied to the same real people and years (William the Conqueror 1087 and 1090, Charlemagne 814 and 815). The relation is made up so that its name does not bring the real single value of a death year; the years are given in the prompt. The edit is stated positively ('can be moth-keyed in more than one year'), as in the revision, and the negation asks whether that cannot happen (no). Side facts and the near and far unrelated queries are those of the revision record. Yes and no are balanced over the topic: the direct question, the first instance and both cross-lingual prompts are no; the second instance asks whether a second year is consistent (yes).
